Upon installation, they execute a malicious preinstall script that downloads and runs a Windows shortcut (.lnk) file, which in turn executes a PowerShell script to bypass UAC and exfiltrate user credentials. This behavior is entirely unrelated to the expected functionality of the legitimate packages and constitutes a severe supply chain attack targeting developer environments.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At runtime, the code performs a deep merge using jQuery.extend(true, ...) with user-controlled input containing a __proto__ property, resulting in the devMode property being set on Object.prototype and making it globally accessible.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code allows user input to modify the Object prototype, which can introduce attacker-controlled properties globally and compromise application logic or security boundaries.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, deep merging should only affect the target object, not the global prototype chain. Here, untrusted input is able to pollute the prototype, impacting all objects.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Deep merging of configuration objects is common, but should never allow modification of the prototype chain.
key_indicators: Use of __proto__ property in user input
Recursive merge without filtering prototype keys
Global side effects such as {}.devMode === true

package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of jQuery allow prototype pollution via the extend() API. Attackers can inject properties into the Object prototype by supplying objects with __proto__, constructor, or prototype keys as input to deep merge operations. This enables privilege escalation, denial of service, or arbitrary code path manipulation in applications that use jQuery.extend(true, ...) with untrusted input, as malicious properties become globally accessible on all objects.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks if the application is running on an allow-listed domain (such as 'vue-admin-beautiful.com'); if not, it recursively deletes all files in the current working directory using fs.rmdirSync, resulting in application disruption and data loss.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs a domain check and, if the environment does not match the allow-list, executes a destructive filesystem operation that deletes all project files. Such behavior is highly abnormal and dangerous in any npm package.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages should never conditionally delete user files based on the runtime domain or environment. This violates user trust and can cause irreversible data loss.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: While kill-switch or self-destruct logic may be used in proprietary DRM or anti-piracy software, it is never appropriate in open source or general-purpose npm packages, especially without explicit user consent.
key_indicators: Conditional logic that checks window.location.host or process.env for specific domains
Use of fs.rmdirSync or similar recursive file deletion APIs
Destructive actions triggered outside of an allow-listed environment
Hidden or obfuscated code in main entry points (e.g., index.js) that is not documented

malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Domain and environment variable checks are sometimes used for licensing enforcement or feature gating, but legitimate implementations do not destroy the user interface or application functionality as a consequence.

malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages should never conditionally delete user files based on the runtime domain or environment. This violates user trust and can cause irreversible data loss.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: While kill-switch or self-destruct logic may be used in proprietary DRM or anti-piracy software, it is never appropriate in open source or general-purpose npm packages, especially without explicit user consent.

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for new or modified GitHub Actions workflows that serialize and POST secrets or variables to external domains. Scan for mass changes to JavaScript files, especially for obfuscated code that injects remote scripts from send.wagateway.pro. Detect client-side code that attaches event listeners to password forms and exfiltrates credentials. Flag any network traffic to send.wagateway.pro domains as a high-confidence indicator of compromise.
